briefdescription.para: Nonlocal viscosity $ \eta $ of the nonlocal balance.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the state variable array.

simplesect.para: Nonlocal viscosity, the damping coefficient of the damped hyperbolic (or, with zero micro-inertia, parabolic) balance \[ m_k\,\ddot{\bar{N}} + \eta\,\dot{\bar{N}} + \bar{N} - c\,\nabla^2\bar{N} = L(\boldsymbol{F},\,\bar{N}) . \]

Zero by default, which is the quasi-static model. Unlike the small-strain Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic::getNonlocalViscosity, which is pure virtual, this default lets existing derived classes keep compiling without answering it. Appended at the very end of the class, after every other virtual, together with getNonlocalMicroInertia() below, so that a stale-library ABI mismatch is confined to callers of these two methods.

briefdescription.para: Nonlocal micro-inertia $ m_k $ of the nonlocal balance.

parameterdescription.para: Pointer to the state variable array.

simplesect.para: The default is zero, the quasi-static model in which the nonlocal field is first order in time and integrated by its viscosity alone the behaviour of every material that predates this method. A derived class opts in to the damped hyperbolic balance by overriding this, mirroring Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic::getNonlocalMicroInertia.

briefdescription.para: Abstract base class for gradient-enhanced (implicit-gradient) materials in the finite strain regime.

detaileddescription.para: The finite-strain counterpart of Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic: the displacement field is coupled to a single scalar nonlocal field $ \bar{N} $ governed by the additional balance equation \[ \bar{N} - c\,\nabla^2\bar{N} = L(\boldsymbol{F},\,\bar{N}), \qquad c = R^2, \] where $ L $ is the local driving force reported in ConstitutiveResponse::L and $ R $ the nonlocal radius reported in ConstitutiveResponse::nonLocalRadius.

simplesect.para: The nonlocal balance is formulated in the material (reference) configuration. Consumers take the gradients with respect to $ \boldsymbol{X} $ and integrate over the reference volume, so $ c $ is a material constant and is neither pushed forward nor weighted by $ J $. The stress, in contrast, is the Kirchhoff stress $ \boldsymbol{\tau} = J\,\boldsymbol{\sigma} $, which is what integrating against the reference volume requires.

The interface carries a single scalar nonlocal field, unlike the small-strain Marmot::Materials::MaterialGradientEnhancedHypoElastic, which is templated on the number of nonlocal variables. It also has **no slot for $ \partial c/\partial\bar{N} $**: a material with damage-dependent interactions (see MarmotDecreasingInteractions) can report the current $ c $, but not its derivative, so its consistent tangent would be incomplete.

Member names, struct shapes and call signatures are fixed by the consumers of this interface (GradientEnhancedFiniteStrainMaterialPoint / ...Particle / ...DisplacementElement), including the six-argument ConstitutiveResponse constructor.
